* fix: make the how-it-works page reachable and add structured data

Search Console shows 4 pages indexed and 5 absent. Indexing tracks internal
link count almost exactly:

  /download  7 links   indexed        /accessibility     3   not
  /privacy   5 links   indexed        /world             1   not
  /creature  4 links   indexed        /architecture-map  1   not
                                      /agent-system      1   not
                                      /how-it-works      0   NOT

/how-it-works had no inbound link anywhere on the site. Every other
occurrence of that string was a stylesheet name, a test, a comment, or <code>
prose. The most commercially useful page on the site was unreachable, while a
doodle short film and the privacy policy were indexed.

It now appears in the shared footer, the homepage's own footer row, and one
descriptive in-content link in the hero. /agent-system and /architecture-map
gain footer links too.

Also here:

- SoftwareApplication JSON-LD on the homepage; the site had no structured data
  at all. No aggregateRating — there are no real reviews, and inventing one is
  both a Google penalty and a lie.
- Titles carry a searchable phrase; the joke moves to openGraph.title, which
  is what people actually see when a link is shared. <title> is the strongest
  on-page signal and "please hire him" matches nothing anyone types.
- The six pages that declared no openGraph.images now reuse the existing card.

The sitemap has also been submitted in Search Console — it was generated and
served correctly since #922 but had never been read, which is why the orphans
were never discovered despite robots.txt declaring it.

wide card — the asset was added without the field that decides how it renders.

head_commit.message:
feat: offer reasoning effort per model and fix embedding re-indexing (#933)

* feat: offer reasoning effort per model and fix embedding re-indexing

Re-indexing embeddings reported success while writing nothing. The input was
truncated to a fixed character budget that overflows a dense language's token
window, every provider error was swallowed, and the batch completed regardless,
so the status strip correctly read 0 indexed under two success toasts. Input is
now chunked and mean-pooled so the whole document is embedded, the working size
is learned once per document and bounded, and a run that embeds nothing fails.

Gemini's default embedding model had been retired by Google, and changing the
code default fixed nothing because the resolved name is persisted, so a
migration rewrites it and evicts the caches keyed on it. Stored vectors carry a
format version, since pooled vectors are not comparable with the truncated
ones written before this change.

The effort setting reached only the Codex agent; every HTTP adapter dropped it.
It is now gated on the per-model reasoning capability, and the levels a picker
offers come from the backend per model, because providers publish different
vocabularies per model and an unsupported value is rejected outright. Parameter
shapes were taken from current provider documentation rather than assumed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: keep the learned chunk size and validate the effort level per model

The size learned for a document was clamped to each chunk's leftover tail and
then carried into the next chunk, so one short remainder shrank the working
size for the rest of the document. A long resume then spent its whole call
budget and failed with a misleading message after embedding a few percent of
its text. The learned size is now lowered only by a real rejection from the
provider.

The level a gemini model accepts varies by model, and the setting is stored per
provider, so switching models within gemini carried a level the new model
rejects straight to the api. The request builder now checks the level against
the model's own table rather than only against the model generation.

Usage is accumulated as work happens rather than returned only on success, so
calls already billed before a partial failure still reach the spend ledger.

Also removes a model from the one click list that the vendor has since shut
down, which this branch had added, and records against each hardcoded model
list which vendor page it was checked against and when, since all three stale
model defects on this branch came from lists that were correct when written.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: give the adaptive embedding path its own module

Adding the chunking and pooling work nearly doubled the provider module, which
is meant to be the trait, registry and shared types rather than a home for a
subsystem. The adaptive path moves to its own file unchanged, and the two
adapter modules that also crossed the size limit move their tests to sibling
files, matching the pattern anthropic already used.

No behaviour changes and no test lost: the same three thousand and ten tests
pass, and the architecture rules pass without adding a single exemption, since
an allowlist entry here would only have hidden the thing the rule exists to
report.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: replace the retired gemini models and validate anthropic effort per model

Three of the four curated gemini entries were dead: the first one, which is the
onboarding default, had been shut down, and two others no longer appear on the
vendor's model page at all. A previous round replaced only the single dead id it
already knew about and left its neighbours unchecked, so the note in that file
now says to verify every entry when re-checking, not just the one being changed.

Anthropic's effort levels turned out not to be uniform either: the vocabulary
has five values and the top two exclude different model sets, so the send path
now checks the level against the model's own table the same way gemini does.
Openai's enum has grown too, but its guide defers the per model breakdown to
individual model pages rather than one table, so only the values verified as
universal are offered and the gate is there for when that changes.

A re-index whose job finished before react committed the state holding its id
left the panel stuck, because the event handler read the id from a closure that
had not updated yet. The id is now held in a ref written before the state.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: stop injecting a temperature gemini 3 asks us not to set

The request builders substituted a default temperature whenever the caller had
not chosen one, and that substituted value is below the figure google asks for
on gemini 3, where lowering it risks looping and degraded output on exactly the
reasoning heavy work this app does. Moving the onboarding default onto a gemini
3 model made that the path every new user takes, so the fix belongs with it.

A value the user actually chose is still sent on any model. Only the invented
one is dropped, and only where the vendor asks for its own default. Applied at
all four call sites rather than the one reported, including company research,
where the hardcoded figure was furthest from what is recommended.

The re-index test now asserts the panel leaves its working state rather than
only that a toast fired, so dropping the clear would fail it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: let the chunker own length policy instead of the ollama adapter

The chunker grows its per chunk size for a long document so the number of
chunks stays bounded, and the ollama adapter still cut anything over eight
thousand characters before sending it. A long resume was therefore silently
truncated again, by a different route, inside the change whose purpose was to
stop that, while the log line beside it claimed no text is dropped.

The adapter no longer rewrites what it is given. Its own over length error is
already recognised, so a chunk that really is too large now comes back as a
failure the halving ladder handles, which is what that ladder is for. The body
builder is now a pure function so a grown chunk can be asserted to arrive whole
without a network mock.

Also gates the ollama thinking parameter against the levels it accepts, the way
the other three adapters already do, and checks the embedding dimension the api
actually returns rather than trusting the request shape, since two careful
readings of the vendor reference disagreed about it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: warn when local ollama has no account key for company research

Company research on local Ollama needs a free Ollama account key, because

the failure, so a missing key looked exactly like "found nothing" and the cover
letter was generated ungrounded with no signal.

The interview-questions modal already warned about this. That predicate moves
into a shared hook and the same non-blocking hint now appears beside the
research toggle in the tailor flow, reusing the existing translation. The hint
is announced, since the provider picker sits directly above it and changing
providers makes the hint appear in response to the user's own action.

head_commit.message:
fix: keep project links out of the resume header and make them work (#931)

* fix: keep project links out of the resume header and make them work

Three defects from one generated resume.

Project sites were swept into the contact profile's extra links at import, so
the exported header rendered them on the contact line and again in PROJECTS.
Only platform profiles may seed extra links now, and website selection prefers
an apex over its own subdomains so it no longer depends on the order links
appear in the source PDF.

PROJECTS items read as "Name - same-name-slug" with no hyperlinks, because the
prompt asked for that shape and injection matched the machine label literally
while the PDF extractor humanised it differently. Items now carry their real
name, matching is normalised and assigns each link to its best line, job-board
and non-personal profile URLs are dropped rather than becoming invented
projects, and a link that still matches nothing is placed in the localized
projects section or left alone rather than appended as an orphan.

The header shown in the editor differed from the exported one, and edits to it
were silently discarded from PDF and DOCX while still shipping in TXT and
clipboard copy. The document text now owns the header at export; the profile
seeds it at generation and fills only what the text leaves blank. See

head_commit.message:
fix: upload only our own debug files to sentry (#930)

* fix: upload only our own debug files to sentry

The first real release run uploaded 474 debug files per matrix leg, ~1900 per
release: dependency build scripts, proc-macro .so files, ring/aws-lc-sys
object files, and every third-party system library bundled into the AppImage —
all to symbolicate one binary. Cause was pointing sentry-cli at the whole
target/ tree.

Scope it to the ajh_tauri* artifacts under release/deps. The paths come from
that run's logs rather than inference, which mattered: on every platform the
debug artifacts use the LIBRARY name (ajh_tauri, underscore) and live in
deps/, not the bin name at release/ajh-tauri. A guessed
release/ajh-tauri.dSYM would have missed the macOS debug companion entirely
and uploaded a binary with no symbols.

Guard the per-triple directory behind a non-empty check — with no triple the
path collapses to the same dir and enumerates everything twice. Verified by
simulating all three layouts: 2 files each, debug companion included, and an
empty match still fails loudly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: assert the debug companion is present, not just some artifact

Review noted the empty-check proves some ajh_tauri* file was found, not that
the file needed to symbolicate the shipped binary is there. Finding
ajh_tauri.exe while its .pdb is missing would pass and still ship
unresolvable stack traces — the same looks-fine-reports-nothing shape this
feature keeps producing.

Assert the companion each platform actually emits, taken from the release
run's uploaded-file list rather than assumed: .pdb on Windows, .dSYM on
macOS, and nothing on Linux where DWARF stays inside the binary. Verified the
positive and negative case for each.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
